plan.summary: Total IEEPA duty paid is $243,524 with $14,948 interest; $145,551 (89 entries) is reachable now through CAPE. $25,226 across 12 entries is urgent (soonest deadline in 3 days), $47,467 needs protests before 180‑day deadlines, $32,499 requires court action, and $15,912 is blocked awaiting CBP guidance.

steps.do: File CAPE for the 12 urgent entries ($25,226 total) before their 80‑day deadlines expire — first is Q7Z‑4101104‑9 ($1,810) due in 3 days.
Confirm your refund bank account in ACE; CBP held 20,362 approved refunds (~$1.1B) for missing details as of Oct 2 — your $145,551 could sit there.
Resolve 3 open protests (Q7Z‑4103107‑0 $2,048, Q7Z‑4103142‑7 $1,853, Q7Z‑4103424‑9 $1,005): if IEEPA‑only and within 80 days of liquidation, withdraw and file CAPE; otherwise keep protest.
File Post Summary Corrections for 2 entries (Q7Z‑4103309‑2 $3,248, Q7Z‑4103339‑9 $2,450) then file CAPE — PSC is blocked once CAPE accepts.
File CAPE for the 87 “cape_now” entries ($132,273 principal) — no hard deadline but every day risks liquidation starting the 80‑day clock.
File protests for 38 protest‑track entries ($47,133) before their 180‑day deadlines per the weekly schedule (next protest deadline week of 2026‑10‑26: 1 entry, $1,693).
Prepare CIT court filings for 31 litigation‑track entries ($29,798) — earliest cited deadlines are Feb 1‑4, 2027.

watch_outs: Missing bank account: CBP pays refunds only electronically; 20,362 refunds (~$1.1B) were stuck as of Oct 2 — your $145,551 could join them.
Surety‑paid entries (2 entries, $1,590): CBP says do not file in CAPE; no surety refund process exists yet — tell your surety.
Someone else holds the claim (3 entries, $2,969): you weren’t the importer of record (courier/forwarder/supplier) — may need assignment or counsel.
Warehouse entry Q7Z‑4103424‑9 ($1,005, type 21/22): CAPE rejects these since Jul 7; file withdrawal entries (types 31/32/34/38) instead.

explanations.Q7Z-4103455-3: This entry (Q7Z-4103455-3) has $1,520 in principal plus $88.11 interest stuck on an AD/CVD suspension. File the refund request in CAPE now so the IEEPA duties come off, but the actual money won’t arrive until Commerce lifts the suspension. There’s no deadline shown, so act promptly to get in line. The uncertain part is when Commerce will lift the suspension — that timing controls when you’re paid.
explanations.Q7Z-4103309-2: This entry requires a Post Summary Correction (PSC) to be filed and accepted before you can submit a CAPE claim for the IEEPA refund. You must file the PSC first; once CAPE accepts the entry, the PSC option is blocked, and the PSC itself cannot claim the refund. The engine shows no deadline or liquidation date, so the timing is uncertain — act promptly to avoid missing any future cutoff. The rule carries a “P” confidence tag, meaning the guidance is plausible but not definitive; confirm with your broker or CBP if needed.
explanations.Q7Z-4101559-4: This entry liquidated on April 30, 2026, putting it in the 81–180 day window where the CAPE refund path is closed. You have **2 days (until October 27, 2026)** to file a protest in ACE to preserve your rights on the $1,567.50 principal plus $125.01 interest. After that, your main option is discussing a Court of International Trade case with counsel, though whether that makes sense for this amount is uncertain. The “P” confidence tag means this is a planning-level view, not a guaranteed outcome.
explanations.K4M-9231751-6: This entry liquidated 81–180 days ago and you are not the importer of record, so any refund belongs to that party and the CAPE path is not available. To preserve rights, you must file a protest in ACE before the 180‑day deadline on 2026‑11‑24 (30 days left) and/or consult counsel about a Court of International Trade case. The liquidation date (2026‑05‑28) is estimated from the entry date and must be confirmed in ACE before acting. Because the importer of record is not you, the $1,046 principal plus $78.24 interest may not be recoverable by your company at all.
explanations.Q7Z-4102801-9: This entry contains only a $530 Section 122 surcharge, which is not eligible for refund through the CAPE/IEEPA process. To preserve any chance of recovery, you (or your broker) must file a protest under 19 U.S.C. § 1514(c)(3) within 180 days of the entry’s liquidation date. Because the liquidation date isn’t provided, the exact protest deadline is unknown — ask your broker or counsel to confirm it immediately. Until that date is confirmed, the ability to act in time remains uncertain.
explanations.Q7Z-4103107-0: Your entry Q7Z-4103107-0 has an open protest, and CAPE will reject any protested entry unless the protest is solely about IEEPA and was filed within 80 days of the June 25 2026 liquidation date. If the protest meets those conditions, you should withdraw it and file a CAPE refund claim promptly; otherwise you should leave the protest in place. The principal at stake is $2,047.50 plus $143.04 interest, but the exact deadline for withdrawal or CAPE filing is uncertain because we don’t know the protest filing date or whether it is IEEPA‑only. Confidence in this guidance is rated probable, so verify the protest details with your broker before acting.
explanations.Q7Z-4103424-9: Your warehouse entry (type 21/22) can no longer be processed in CAPE as of July 7, 2026, so the $1,640 principal plus $69.31 interest will not refund through this entry. You must file withdrawal entries (types 31/32/34/38) instead to recover the duties. No deadline is shown in the data, so confirm the filing window with your broker or ACE account. The rule carries a “P” confidence tag, meaning the guidance may still be subject to change.
explanations.Q7Z-4101104-9: This entry was liquidated on August 9, 2026, making it eligible for a tariff refund under the CAPE program, but CBP must accept the filing within 80 days of liquidation. You have only 3 days left (until October 28, 2026) to file the refund claim in ACE through your broker or directly. The refund would cover $1,810 principal plus $115.34 interest, though the applicability of the “India (Russian oil)” and “Reciprocal” programs is not guaranteed. The rule carries a “P” confidence tag, meaning the interpretation is plausible but not certain; confirm with your broker before filing.
